[MUQATIL:7:10-12/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Iblis claims superiority because he was created from fire and Adam from clay; fire overcomes clay.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ailments commonly use faʿila yafʿalu, with a verbal noun on faʿal and an adjective on faʿil; Sībawayh illustrates the pattern with ḥabiṭa and ḥabija.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Khashiyahu, khashyatan, and khāsh follow a derivational pattern like raḥima and rāḥim, even though the surface forms differ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Opposite states such as arisha, batira, fariḥa, and jaḏila use the same verb, noun, and adjective pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as jaḏlān, kaslān, and sakrān pair with jaḏil, kasil, and sakir, showing related faʿlān and faʿil formations.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nashiṭa has the adjective nashīṭ, while nashāṭ parallels suqām; saqīm and suqām are compared with jamīl and jamāl.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Defects such as sahk and qinam are treated like diseases, with corresponding nouns sahka and qinma.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ʿAqara and ʿāqir follow the same pattern as saqima and sāqim, and māthik provides a parallel adjective.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Khamaṭ is contrasted with qinam, which Sībawayh glosses as sahk.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Arija describes wind movement and brightness, while ḥamisa describes agitation and anger; these share a semantic group of arousal.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Aḥmasa occurs alongside ḥamisa; in this group afʿal functions like faʿlān, as in ghaḍbān.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Afʿal can also join faʿlān forms and generally keeps the same verb and verbal-noun pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The adjective may instead be faʿīl, as in mariḍa yamraḍu and marīḍ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو الخطاب | reports | Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports that ahyam and haymān both mean thirsty.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Salis, qaliq, naziq, and ghaliq are grouped with agitation because they denote lightness and movement.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ghaliq can describe nonhuman things too, since they have become light or loose in their place.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Unpleasant qualities such as ʿasr, shakās, laqas, and laḥaz follow faʿila yafʿalu with faʿil adjectives because their meanings resemble ailments.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Saqima and ʿasura can both yield faʿīl adjectives; nakida has both nakid and an-kad, and laḥija is close in meaning to ʿasura.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Laḥija is included in the same group because its meaning is close to ʿusr.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Saqima may be said with kasra or by some Arabs with fatḥa, compared with karuma and karīm.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Saqm and ḥuzn are verbal nouns; ḥuzn is grouped with disease because it is an affliction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Wajila and similar states of fear follow the same verb and noun pattern because they are close in meaning to wajiʿa.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Blindness of the heart is treated as an affliction that strikes the heart.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Fear and terror verbs such as faziʿa, fariqa, wajila, and wajira use this pattern because fear reaches the heart as illness reaches the body.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Awjara joins the faʿila pattern in a related sense; faʿila and afʿala can coexist, as in other paired adjective patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجعيوجعوجعاوهووجعلتقارب#671/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Farriqtuhu and fazzaʿtuhu mean farriqtu minhu and faziʿtu minhu; the preposition min has been omitted.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some verbs can take two direct objects, though a speaker may stop after the first or continue with a second object.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With sammaytu and kannaytu, bāʾ works as in ʿaraftuhu bi-Zaydin; the prepositional construction differs in meaning from the direct-object construction.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Farazdaq's ikhtīra al-rijāla shows the direct-object construction with ikhtāra.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Farazdaq also uses nubbiʾtu ʿAbda Allāhi bi-l-jawwi as an example of a verb taking its complement through bāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | This treatment is limited: verbs do not all permit preposition deletion, and verbs do not all take one or two objects.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Choosing someone from a group can take two direct objects after the preposition is omitted; Sībawayh cites Qur'an 7:155 as an example. | mentions 7:155
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Naming and giving a kunya can take two objects; daʿawtuhu takes two only when it means naming, while calling someone to an action takes one.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Many such verbs originally govern a phrase introduced by a preposition; when the preposition is omitted, the verb governs the complement directly.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An unnamed poet's astaghfiru Allāha dhanban represents astaghfiru Allāha min dhanbin, with min omitted.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib's amartuka al-khayr means amartuka bi-l-khayr, with bāʾ omitted.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Mutalammis's ālaytu ḥubb al-ʿIrāq means ālaytu ʿalā ḥubb al-ʿIrāq, with ʿalā omitted.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nubbiʾtu Zaydan means 'I was told about Zayd'; ʿan and ʿalā do not omit like bāʾ, nor does min in a positive clause.
[SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتاقتصرتعلىالمفعولالأولإنشئت#22/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Astaghfiru Allāha dhanban and amartuka al-khayr are uncommon constructions used only by some speakers.

[FARRA:v1p373/r6] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | Arabic can repeat a negative particle for emphasis, as in ما إن رأينا; Qurʾanic parallels include the cited clauses in 6:109, 21:95, and 57:29. | mentions 6:109, 21:95, 57:29

[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#6/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | The question means what prevented you from prostrating; lā is extra, for the reason explained in Taʾwīl Mushkil al-Qurʾān.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p153/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | The لا is extra; the intended question is what prevented Iblis from prostrating, with the added negative reflecting that he did not.
[TAB-FULL:v10p81/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God asks Iblis what kept him from refraining from prostration to Adam when commanded; the question concerns his disobedient refusal.
[TAB-FULL:v10p81/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Iblis was blamed for disobeying God by leaving prostration, not for prostrating; Tabari explains how the wording can express that charge.
[TAB-FULL:v10p81/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض نحويي البصرة | reports | Some Basran grammarians take لا as extra, so the question means what prevented you from prostrating; they cite the poetic phrase أبى جوده لا البخل.
[TAB-FULL:v10p81/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · يونس | reports | Yunus reports that Abu ʿAmr makes البخل genitive and treats لا as annexed to it, since لا can name either generosity or miserliness.
[TAB-FULL:v10p81/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض نحويي الكوفة | reports | Some Kufan grammarians also take لا as extra but say it repeats the negation for emphasis because the preceding verse says Iblis was not among the prostrators. | mentions 7:11
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض نحويي الكوفة | reports | The Kufan explanation treats لا as a repeated negation, with the poem’s إن reinforcing the earlier ما.
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض نحويي البصرة | reports | Another grammarian says لا is neither extra nor a particle of connection: منع means ‘say,’ so the question is who told Iblis not to prostrate.
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض من روى | reports | One transmitter interprets لا in the poem أبى جوده لا البخل as the word for miserliness itself.
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعضهم | reports | Some explain منع as blocking a person from what he wants and thus compelling him to do the opposite, so the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Tabari supplies an ellipsis: ‘What prevented you from prostrating and made you need not to?’ The suppressed أحوجك is understood from the statement that Iblis was not among the prostrators. | mentions 7:11
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | rejects | Tabari rejects treating لا as meaningless padding, since every word in the Qur’an has a sound meaning.
[TAB-FULL:v10p83/r7] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | rejects | Tabari rejects taking منع as a command to leave prostration: a person able to obey or disobey is not prevented from acting, and Iblis would not obey another’s command after defying God.
[TAB-FULL:v10p85/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Iblis claimed that he was better than Adam, stronger and more powerful because he was made from fire and Adam from clay.
[TAB-FULL:v10p85/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Tabari says fire’s lightness, impetuosity, instability, and upward motion fed Iblis’s arrogance, while clay’s steadiness, patience, forbearance, modesty, and deliberation led Adam to repent and seek forgiveness; their outcomes followed prior divine decree.
[TAB-FULL:v10p85/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الحسن وابن سيرين | reports | Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin call Iblis the first to make an erroneous analogy; Ibn Sirin adds that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogical reasoning.
[TAB-FULL:v10p85/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن سيرين | reports | Ibn Sirin says Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogies.
[TAB-FULL:v10p85/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Iblis’s analogy ignored Adam’s honors: God created him with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, commanded the angels to prostrate to him, taught him the names, and granted him many further distinctions.
[TAB-FULL:v10p87/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says Iblis was the first to make an analogy.
[TAB-FULL:v10p87/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reports that God ordered the angels accompanying Iblis to prostrate to Adam; all did except Iblis, who arrogantly claimed to be better, older, and stronger because fire is stronger than clay.
[TAB-FULL:v10p87/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says that after Iblis was created from fire, his descendants were made from water.
[TAB-FULL:v10p87/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Tabari says Iblis did not directly answer what prevented him from prostrating; instead, he began boasting that he was better than Adam, indirectly revealing the reason.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r10] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | ما is nominative as the interrogative subject: what prevented you? No explicit answer is given because the question itself conveys it.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The لا is emphatic and omitted in sense, so the question means ما منعك أن تسجد.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Although God knew the cause, the question rebukes Iblis and exposes his defiant disobedience.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Anyone who disobeys God's command while denying that it is obligatory is an unbeliever by consensus; denying prayer's obligation is the example.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Iblis's refusal was defiant unbelief, unlike Adam and Eve, who confessed their sin and repented; Iblis persisted without repentance. | mentions 7:23
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r6] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The same treatment of لا applies in لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب, where the meaning is لأن يعلم أهل الكتاب. | mentions 57:29
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r7] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · قالوا | reports | For the cited verse, they explain أبى جوده لا البخل to mean that his generosity rejected miserliness.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r8] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · أبو عمرو بن العلاء | prefers | Abu Amr reports the line as أبى جوده البخل; he explains لا as what makes a person miserly and نعم as assent to continue giving.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r9] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | prefers | Al-Zajjaj offers another parse: لا is not redundant, and البخل is accusative as a substitute for لا.
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · الواسطي | reports | Al-Wasiti warns that relying on ritual observances in both worlds makes ignorance a home, objection a trait, and distance from God its outcome; seeing worship as one's own act is dangerous self-regard.
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | One explanation says Iblis saw his substance and worship and thought himself superior; self-regard in one's acts corrupts the soul.
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · قيل | reports | Another says Iblis's self-assertion alone brought the curse: nothing distanced him more than seeing himself. | mentions 7:13
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · قيل | reports | A further gloss says Iblis mistook created substance and origin for superiority, failing to recognize that merit comes from the Bestower rather than one's essence.
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · الواسطي | reports | Al-Wasiti says wearing the garment of ritual practice makes the ego's claim of I arise; even without saying better, Iblis would have been ruined by asserting I in comparison.
[SULAMI:v1p221#3/r6] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | Ibn Ata says pride in himself veiled Iblis from revering God; when the Real dominates a heart, it leaves no room to exalt anyone else.
[THALABI:v4p217#2/r11] THALABI, d. 427 · بعضهم | reports | Some grammarians treat لا as extra and إن as a connective, yielding “what kept you from prostrating to Adam”; they cite a parallel construction in 21:95. | mentions 21:95
[THALABI:v4p218/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · قال الشاعر | reports | A poetic citation is offered for the construction أن لا, with the author glossing it as أن alone.
[THALABI:v4p218/r10] THALABI, d. 427 · الحكماء | reports | A second argument is that clay gathers things together whereas fire separates them.
[THALABI:v4p218/r11] THALABI, d. 427 · الحكماء | reports | A third argument says the reported soil of Paradise is fragrant musk, while no report says Paradise contains fire or Hell contains soil.
[THALABI:v4p218/r12] THALABI, d. 427 · الحكماء | reports | A fourth argument is that fire causes torment and is God’s punishment for His enemies, while soil does not cause torment.
[THALABI:v4p218/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · آخر | reports | A second unnamed poet supplies another cited example containing أن لا in the discussion of the construction.
[THALABI:v4p218/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · آخر | reports | The poet’s phrase أبى جوده لا البخل is glossed as أبى جوده البخل: his generosity refused stinginess.
[THALABI:v4p218/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب | reports | Some disliked the form القالا and interpreted منع as saying, since speech and action can both prevent; the construction means who said to you not to prostrate?
[THALABI:v4p218/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · بعضهم | reports | Another explanation defines prevention as standing between someone and what they want, so the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
